name: Meta-ExternalFetcher
follows_en: Partial, may bypass robots.txt because fetches are requested by a user

ips.note: Meta's crawler page does not list IP addresses or a verification method for this crawler; it identifies the crawler by its user-agent string.

vendor_quote: The Meta-ExternalFetcher crawler fetches individual links at a user's request and supports product functions such as evaluating and improving agentic AI capabilities—including helping AI navigate websites to complete tasks for users. Accordingly, this crawler may bypass robots.txt rules.
what_en: Meta-ExternalFetcher is a Meta crawler that fetches individual links at a user's request. Meta says it supports product functions such as evaluating and improving agentic AI capabilities, including helping AI navigate websites to complete tasks for users. Meta documents it alongside Meta-ExternalAgent, Meta-WebIndexer, Meta-ExternalAds and FacebookExternalHit on one page.
block_en: Meta says you can block its crawlers by adding a disallow for the relevant crawler to robots.txt. Meta also says Meta-ExternalFetcher may bypass robots.txt because it performs fetches that were requested by the user. Meta says changes to robots.txt can take up to 24 hours to take effect because crawlers may cache the file for up to 24 hours.
compare_en: Meta-ExternalAgent crawls the web in the background, including for training foundation AI models, while Meta-ExternalFetcher fetches single links a user asked for and may bypass robots.txt.
notes: Meta page shows UA forms 'meta-externalfetcher/1.1 (+/documentation/sharing/webmasters/web-crawlers)' and 'meta-externalfetcher/1.1'; the first has a relative URL as published, so the bare form is recorded. Page lists no IPs for this crawler. Hint URL redirects to the /documentation/ URL used here. The page's robots.txt example does not include meta-externalfetcher.
answer_en: Meta-ExternalFetcher is a Meta crawler that fetches individual links at a user's request. Meta says it supports product functions such as helping AI navigate websites to complete tasks for users, and that it may bypass robots.txt because the fetches are requested by a user. Robots.txt changes can take up to 24 hours.
